output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.UnzipEngine#getOutputFileNameWithPath() built the extraction target by naive string concatenation of the caller's outPath with the attacker-controlled entry name (fileHeader.getFileName() or a caller-supplied newFileName), with no check that the result stayed inside outPath. That single unsanitized path fed three sinks in getOutputStream() (parent-dir mkdirs, exists()/delete(), and the FileOutputStream write) as well as the applyFileAttributes call site in unzipFile() (line 93), all named in the alert's traces.

Fix: added a new static helper, Zip4jUtil.checkPathIsContainedInRoot(rootPath, entryOutputPath, entryName), that resolves both the extraction root and the candidate output path with File#getCanonicalPath() (which normalizes "..", mixed separators, and resolves symlinks) and throws a ZipException unless the candidate is the root itself or a canonical descendant of it. This is invoked once inside UnzipEngine#getOutputFileNameWithPath(), so every caller of that method — the getOutputStream() write path and the applyFileAttributes call — is covered by one check, matching all three "vulnerabilities" entries in the alert (mkdirs, delete/overwrite, FileOutputStream write) and both traversal encodings shown (with/without the intermediate `file` variable in the trace).

Also hardened the two sibling call sites in net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.Unzip.java that build the same class of unsanitized path outside of UnzipEngine and were not covered by the above fix: the directory-entry mkdirs() branch in initExtractFile() (fileHeader.isDirectory() == true, which never reaches UnzipEngine) and checkOutputDirectoryStructure()'s parent-directory mkdirs() for file entries (which runs before UnzipEngine.unzipFile() and would otherwise still create arbitrary escaped directories even though the subsequent file write would later be blocked). Both now call the same Zip4jUtil.checkPathIsContainedInRoot() helper before touching the filesystem.

This blocks: relative "../" traversal at any depth, traversal via a caller-supplied newFileName (same helper, same trust boundary), and symlinked-root escapes (canonicalization resolves existing symlinks). Absolute-path entries are already contained by the pre-existing string-concatenation behavior (outPath + separator + fileName lexically nests under outPath) and are additionally caught by the canonical-path check as a defense-in-depth measure.

Regression coverage: added src/test/java/net/lingala/zip4j/ZipSlipRegressionTest.java, a dependency-free (no JUnit is wired into this pom.xml) class with a main() method that (1) builds a zip with a ".." traversal file entry and asserts extraction throws and no file lands outside the destination, (2) does the same for a ".." traversal directory entry (covering the Unzip.java fix), and (3) extracts a normal nested-path zip and asserts it still succeeds and lands in the right place, guarding against over-restrictive regressions. Verified: build succeeds (mvn -B -DskipTests package), the provided POV script (.security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) now exits 1 / "NOT VULNERABLE" against the patched build (was exit 0 / "VULNERABLE" before), and the new regression class prints PASS for all three checks.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: extraction of any archive entry whose resolved path would land outside the destination directory now throws ZipException instead of silently writing/deleting outside the root — this is the intended fix but is a breaking behavior change for any (unusual) caller that relied on the old traversal-permissive behavior. getCanonicalPath() does I/O (resolves the real filesystem path) and can itself throw IOException, which is wrapped into ZipException; on filesystems/paths where canonicalization behaves unexpectedly (e.g. certain network mounts) this could in theory reject a legitimate path, though this is the standard, widely-used mitigation pattern for zip-slip (e.g. same approach used by many other libraries). No dependency or build-config changes were made. The new test file is plain Java (no JUnit) since the project's pom.xml has no test framework dependency; mvn test still succeeds (surefire finds the *Test-named class but runs 0 tests since it has no JUnit-recognized methods), so it doesn't break existing CI wiring — the meaningful verification is via the javac/java regression_commands provided.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 Zip Slip in zip4j by adding a centralized canonical-path containment check that rejects any archive-entry-derived output path that resolves outside the caller-supplied extraction root, before any mkdirs/delete/write happens.
